notes: Use a Navigo Easy with a t+ carnet on the metro, the RER C for Versailles and the RER B for CDG (11 EUR). The city is walkable: skip the metro for 20-minute distances.
Timed online tickets are essential for the Louvre, Orsay and Sainte-Chapelle. The Louvre is closed on Tuesdays and Orsay on Mondays. The Paris Museum Pass covers 2 to 6 days.
Winter temperatures are 3-8°C and it is dark by 17:00. Museums are quiet, with Christmas windows (Galeries Lafayette) and mulled wine markets in December.
Bistro lunch menus (formule) cost 18-25 EUR, half the evening price. Tap water (carafe d'eau) is free; round up the bill as a tip.
Bouillons (Chartier, Racine) are cheap classics. Go to the Marais for falafel, and to Pain Pain or Du Pain et des Idées for croissants.
Watch out for pickpockets on metro line 1 and in Montmartre. Wear your backpack on your front.

transit.name: Navigo Easy / t+ carnet
transit.why_chosen: Covers the metro, RER and buses. The 10-ticket carnet is the most practical option; Versailles needs an extra RER C ticket.
transit.coverage: Paris metro, otobüs, tramvay, RER zone 1
transit.where_to_buy: Metro istasyonları biletmatik; Navigo Easy kartı 2 EUR

days.theme: Louvre, Tuileries and the Eiffel Tower

stops.name: Louvre Müzesi
stops.tips: Head straight for the Mona Lisa, then the Denon wing. Book a timed ticket online (32 EUR for non-EU visitors); the Carrousel entrance has no queue.

stops.name: Jardin des Tuileries
stops.tips: Stroll through the gardens from the Louvre to Concorde, and grab one of the green chairs.

stops.name: Café Kitsuné Palais Royal
stops.tips: Coffee and a sandwich in the Palais Royal garden, set in a colonnaded courtyard.

stops.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
stops.tips: Monet's Water Lilies in oval rooms. Right next to the Louvre and calm.

stops.name: Eiffel Tower
stops.tips: Take the stairs to the 2nd floor, then the lift to the summit (about 29 EUR). Book online, go at sunset, and take photos from Trocadéro.

backups.name: Le Petit Cler
backups.tips: A bistro on Rue Cler, close to the Eiffel Tower.

backups.name: Champ de Mars
backups.tips: Lawns beneath the tower: picnic here and watch the light show (every hour on the hour).

days.theme: Île de la Cité, Latin Quarter and Saint-Germain

stops.name: Notre-Dame de Paris
stops.tips: The restored cathedral is free; reserve a time slot online. Mornings are quiet.

stops.name: Sainte-Chapelle
stops.tips: 1,113 stained-glass panels, loveliest on a sunny morning. Book online.

stops.name: Shakespeare and Company
stops.tips: The legendary English-language bookshop on the Seine.

stops.name: Le Comptoir du Panthéon
stops.tips: A bistro opposite the Panthéon, with steak-frites and a terrace.

stops.name: Panthéon
stops.tips: The tombs of Voltaire, Hugo and Curie, plus the Foucault pendulum.

backups.name: Bouillon Racine
backups.tips: An Art Nouveau bouillon with a cheap, classic French menu.

backups.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
backups.tips: The Senate gardens, with a pond and chairs. Go here instead of the Panthéon.

stops.name: Sacré-Cœur
stops.tips: The basilica is free; the dome costs 8 EUR. The steps are empty in the morning, with views over Paris.

stops.name: Place du Tertre
stops.tips: The painters' square. Portraits cost 40-60 EUR, and the price is negotiable.

stops.name: Montmartre Vineyard and Lapin Agile
stops.tips: Paris's last vineyard and a cabaret, on Rue des Saules.

stops.name: Chantoiseau Montmartre
stops.tips: A neo-bistro 7 minutes from Place du Tertre, with a set lunch menu.

stops.name: Musée de Montmartre
stops.tips: Renoir's studio and gardens, with views over the vineyard.

backups.name: Boulangerie Pain Pain
backups.tips: Award-winning baguettes and pastries for a quick lunch.

backups.name: Moulin Rouge
backups.tips: See it from outside in Pigalle; the evening show is extra (about 120 EUR).

stops.name: Place des Vosges
stops.tips: The oldest square in Paris, with arcades and Victor Hugo's house (free).

stops.name: Musée Picasso Paris
stops.tips: The Picasso collection in the Hôtel Salé. Book online.

stops.name: L'As du Fallafel
stops.tips: The falafel place on Rue des Rosiers with the queue outside. Eat standing up.

stops.name: Marché des Enfants Rouges
stops.tips: The oldest market in Paris, with Moroccan, Japanese and Lebanese stalls.

stops.name: Centre Pompidou
stops.tips: Inside-out architecture, modern art and a terrace with views over Paris. It is under renovation 2025-30: if closed, go to the Bourse de Commerce.

backups.name: Bourse de Commerce Pinault Collection
backups.tips: Tadao Ando's concrete cylinder, with contemporary art. Go here if the Pompidou is closed.

backups.name: Au Petit Versailles du Marais
backups.tips: Award-winning croissants and quiche. Go here instead of the falafel.

stops.name: Musée d'Orsay
stops.tips: Impressionists in a former railway station. Van Gogh is on the 5th floor; take a photo through the clock face. Book online.

stops.name: Rue du Bac & Bon Marché
stops.tips: The Grande Épicerie food hall, good for souvenirs.

stops.name: Café de Flore
stops.tips: Saint-Germain's literary café: croque monsieur and hot chocolate.

stops.name: Pont des Arts and the Seine Banks
stops.tips: See Île de la Cité from the bridge, then walk along the riverside path.

stops.name: Bateaux Parisiens Seine Cruise
stops.tips: A 1-hour river cruise from the Eiffel Tower pier, with Notre-Dame and the Eiffel Tower in sunset light.

backups.name: Bateaux Mouches
backups.tips: The other cruise company, at Pont de l'Alma.

backups.name: La Grande Épicerie de Paris
backups.tips: The food hall at Bon Marché. Have lunch at the counters instead of Café de Flore.

stops.name: Palace of Versailles
stops.tips: 45 minutes on the RER C. Get the palace + gardens + Trianon passport (about 32 EUR). The Hall of Mirrors is empty at the 09:00 opening.

stops.name: Gardens of Versailles
stops.tips: The gardens are free in winter. The fountains are off, so just walk.

stops.name: La Flottille Versailles
stops.tips: A restaurant on the Grand Canal, with boat rental next door.

stops.name: Petit Trianon & Queen's Hamlet
stops.tips: Marie Antoinette's village and the queen's farm, included with the passport.

stops.name: Marché Notre-Dame Versailles
stops.tips: A food market in town: pick up cheese on your way back.

backups.name: Angelina Versailles
backups.tips: Hot chocolate and Mont-Blanc inside the palace.

backups.name: Grand Trianon
backups.tips: A pink marble pavilion. Go here instead of the Petit Trianon.

days.theme: Canal Saint-Martin and a gentle farewell

stops.name: Canal Saint-Martin
stops.tips: Iron footbridges and canal locks. Have a morning coffee and spot the Amélie film scenes.

stops.name: Du Pain et des Idées
stops.tips: One of the best bakeries in Paris. Try the pistachio-chocolate escargot.

stops.name: Marché d'Aligre
stops.tips: A daily market at Bastille, with cheese and edible souvenirs.

stops.name: Le Baron Rouge
stops.tips: A wine bar next to the Aligre market. Oysters and wine from the barrel make a fitting farewell.

stops.name: Gare du Nord
stops.tips: 35 minutes to CDG on the RER B. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Coulée Verte René-Dumont
backups.tips: A green walkway on a former railway line. Go here instead of Aligre.
